notes.text: Timestamps in this queue are date-granular. The authoring role holds no clock, and 00:00:00Z means 'on 2026-09-23'.

Each queue task is exactly one committed or reserved TASK card. No committed card is edited to fit this queue (DEC-20260923-034ba0 R-7 (1)). Where a queue entry differs from its card, the entry's own note says how, and the card governs the agent. The queue governs the dispatcher's ordering, together with DEC-20260923-8b2dbf AA-2.

TASK-20260923-0fa03f and TASK-20260923-4ff597 are each ONE archive task with two receipted commits (precedent TASK-20260923-3b12c2). research_dispatch.py marks an archive completed only with one commit_sha and full path_sha256 coverage (lines 939-948). So each stays `queued` until its PHASE B verifies. Its phase A is recorded in the archive block's `phases` note, and, for 0fa03f, as a verified SUBSET of path_sha256, which the tool allows while an archive is not completed (line 935). When phase B verifies, a revision sets commit_sha to the phase-B commit and parent_sha to its parent, fills path_sha256 for every declared artifact, and marks the archive completed. binding_mode is content_first: every bound file is terminal, and the verifier reads them at HEAD (lines 1832-1850). The phase-B commit message must name the task and every record_id.

Two orderings of DEC-20260923-8b2dbf AA-2 cannot be DAG edges without a cycle, because TASK-20260923-4ff597 archives TASK-20260923-6c7f55, which follows TASK-20260923-cd932c. They are expressed as state `blocked`, which the dispatcher reports as task_marked_blocked. (1) TASK-20260923-cd932c (stage 2) stays blocked until phase A of TASK-20260923-4ff597 verifies (SQ-4, SQ-5). (2) TASK-20260923-6c7f55 (stage 2b) stays blocked until its exact run directories exist in a phase-A-bound trial-plan-v2-a1.json and phase B of TASK-20260923-0fa03f verifies (SQ-7). Each is lifted only by an appended tasks_state_revisions entry citing the verified receipt, never by editing a card. goal_lanes.py claims only `queued` tasks, so a blocked task cannot be claimed early.

artifact_paths must be exact files (research_dispatch.py lines 219-227). A `completed` lane release refuses while a declared artifact is missing (goal_lanes.py cmd_release). So each producer declares only files certain to exist when it completes; directories stay in write_scope. The run-package files of TASK-20260923-cd932c and TASK-20260923-6c7f55, and the file list of implementation-v2-a1/, are not knowable today. The revision that records each archive phase appends them, file by file, from that phase's receipt, before the archive is marked completed. Until then, the receipt is the complete binding and this queue is a floor.

TASK-20260923-cd932c's committed card carries review_required true, and so do TASK-20260923-4c64b5 and TASK-20260923-6c7f55. research_dispatch.py (lines 766-812) therefore requires, for each: an independent reviewer that depends on the producer and on its snapshot archive, and one ledger archive that depends on every review. The chain is declared now, as `blocked` placeholders under identifiers the dispatching session supplied: TASK-20260923-9d6cfc, the review-plan act, written FIRST with its prior (SQ-9); TASK-20260923-ab99ed, its ledger archive, owning DEC-20260923-71ebeb; TASK-20260923-3eb51f (validator), TASK-20260923-4547d3 (red team) and TASK-20260923-60caac (blind re-derivation); TASK-20260923-af2fe6, the evidence-review act; and TASK-20260923-7dba83, the ledger archive of the reviews and of the evidence review, owning DEC-20260923-c6b67b and EV-GFPN-acdec5. None of these cards exists yet. The review-plan act writes them, and may reshape this chain by appended revision (tasks_added / cancelled), never by edit. The placeholders assert only the structure the tool requires.

The tool assigns the reviews to a LEDGER archive. This goal's practice (TASK-20260923-3b12c2 phase B) commits review reports BEFORE any composition, so TASK-20260923-7dba83 is two-phase: phase A snapshots the returned reports (snapshot-receipt.json), then TASK-20260923-af2fe6 composes, then phase B commits the evidence and decision (ledger-receipt.json). TASK-20260923-af2fe6 therefore stays blocked until phase A of TASK-20260923-7dba83 verifies, by the same revision mechanism.

Stage 1 of TASK-20260923-cd932c ran without a lane claim, because no queue existed. That is a disclosed deviation recorded by CORR-20260923-6d8879 (DEC-20260923-034ba0 R-7 stage_1_claimless_launch). This queue holds stage 2 ONLY for that card. Stage 1's outputs are already bound by phase A of TASK-20260923-0fa03f.

ledger/goals/GOAL-GFPN-380702/goal.yaml is owned in this queue by TASK-20260923-33484e (archived content_at_commit by TASK-20260923-58a958), and validate_queue refuses a second owner (line 877). Later checkpoints of this batch (the review-plan act and the evidence-review act) follow GOAL-AUXIN-a93442 BATCH-ba0b0d's ownership ruling. Either they write a write-once shard under ledger/goals/GOAL-GFPN-380702/checkpoints/, which the revision that adds their cards declares, or they disclose the head edit as committed-but-not-hash-bound-by-this-batch.

Before any launch, the dispatching session opens the lane once: `python3 tools/goal_lanes.py open-lane GOAL-GFPN-380702 BATCH-6b1c29 --queue coordination/goals/GOAL-GFPN-380702/batches/BATCH-6b1c29/dispatch_queue.json ...`. Before EACH producer launch, it runs `git fetch`, then `python3 tools/goal_lanes.py lanes GOAL-GFPN-380702`, then `python3 tools/goal_lanes.py claim <this queue> <TASK> --as executor --ttl-minutes N --publish`, and checks the host for other solver processes. On return it runs `release ... --outcome completed|failed|abandoned`. Each archive is claimed as coordinator by the session that commits it where its queue state admits a claim. A claim is a pointer, never a permission (DEC-20260923-034ba0 R-7 (2)-(4)).

This queue was written by a Coordinator subagent without a shell. The dispatching session runs tools/research_dispatch.py and tools/validate_dispatch_reference.py on it before TASK-20260923-58a958's commit, and commits it only if both pass (R-7 (5)). A failure is returned to the Coordinator with the exact error text. If no honest queue can pass, the substitute is recorded under DEC-20260923-f11b13 before any launch (R-7 (6)).
